subject.title: refactor: remove pre-2026.4 compatibility shims and legacy migrations

question: May the next release intentionally require pre-2026.4 users to step through a 2026.6 release and simultaneously remove public aliases and the older daemon updater bridge?
rationale: Source and release history prove these contracts are present in v2026.6.11, but repository policy does not define a minimum directly-upgradable release or authorize this combined breaking boundary; tests cannot decide that support policy.

options.title: Preserve shipped upgrade contracts
options.body: Keep Matrix doctor migration and the daemon bridge, and split public API retirements into explicit deprecation work.

options.title: Approve a minimum upgrade version
options.body: Accept the removals only with a documented supported-version floor plus packaged direct-upgrade, older-updater, and downstream API proof.

options.title: Narrow the cleanup
options.body: Land only private dead-code deletions whose producers and callers are demonstrably outside supported releases.

recommendation.title: Preserve shipped upgrade contracts
recommendation.body: Keep Matrix doctor migration and the daemon bridge, and split public API retirements into explicit deprecation work.

likelyOwner.reason: They defined the cleanup and upgrade contract and have the strongest cross-surface history for deciding whether this breaking release boundary is intentional.
